challenge.exploration_summary: The expressjs repository is a Node.js web framework. The core response API lives in lib/response.js (1053+ lines), which defines the res prototype with methods like res.set, res.append, res.cookie, res.vary, res.redirect, etc. Each method is well-tested under test/res.*.js using mocha + supertest, following a consistent pattern: create an express app, register a middleware that calls the res method, then assert on the response via supertest. The full original test suite (1238 tests across test/ and test/acceptance/) passes with zero failures. I chose lib/response.js because it has excellent test coverage, a clear and stable interface, and a natural gap: there is no convenience helper for assembling the Cache-Control header, which is error-prone to build by hand.
challenge.feature_spec: Adds a new res.cache(options) method to the response prototype that builds a standards-compliant Cache-Control header from a structured options object. Supported directives: maxAge, sMaxAge, staleWhileRevalidate, staleIfError (numeric seconds, floored, non-finite/negative values ignored), public/private (mutually exclusive, private wins), noStore, noCache (boolean or array of header field names), mustRevalidate, proxyRevalidate, noTransform, mustUnderstand, and immutable. Throws TypeError when options is missing or not an object. Defaults to 'no-cache' when no directives are produced. Returns the ServerResponse for chaining and overwrites any previously set Cache-Control header.
challenge.feature_rationale: Setting Cache-Control correctly is a common, error-prone task for web applications. Express currently requires developers to hand-assemble the header string via res.set('Cache-Control', ...). A structured helper that maps individual caching directives to a compliant header value reduces mistakes (e.g. conflicting public/private, malformed no-cache field lists, negative ages) and improves readability. This fits naturally alongside existing header helpers such as res.vary, res.append, and res.set in lib/response.js, and follows the same chainable, options-object conventions used by res.cookie and res.links.
challenge.bug_description: The isFiniteSeconds helper used to validate age directives (maxAge, sMaxAge, staleWhileRevalidate, staleIfError) uses a strict greater-than-zero check (value > 0) instead of greater-than-or-equal (value >= 0). This causes the value 0 to be silently ignored, so directives like max-age=0, s-maxage=0, and stale-while-revalidate=0 are dropped from the Cache-Control header. Since max-age=0 is a common and important directive meaning 'always revalidate before reuse', dropping it can cause caches to serve stale responses when the developer explicitly intended to disable caching, leading to data integrity and security issues.
